Fouquet's Courchevel has a new director of food and beverage. Grégoire Gaillard has led the restaurants and bars of the Barrière palace in Courchevel 1850 since June 2026, and this winter will be his first full season at the helm.

## Every table in the house

His remit covers the whole hotel. First Loulou, the Italian trattoria born in Paris that now has a home on the slopes: truffle pizza, vodka pasta, a dessert buffet, a bar and a terrace, open from breakfast until late, for hotel guests and visitors alike. Then La Table Savoyarde, the hotel's second restaurant, with Savoyard and Italian cooking; the Lounge Bar; Christophe Adam's afternoon tea by the fireplace; and the hotel's caviar club.

Fouquet's Courchevel is a five-star hotel with the Palace distinction and 42 rooms and suites, a 1,000 m² spa and a 20-metre pool. It belongs to the Fouquet's collection of Groupe Barrière.

## A career built in the best houses

Gaillard's path runs through some of the most demanding dining rooms in France and Switzerland. He was maître d'hôtel at Hôtel Barrière Le Majestic in Cannes in 2022, then at Le Chabichou by Stéphane Buron, two MICHELIN stars, in Courchevel during the 2022-23 winter. He moved on to F&B supervisor at the Carlton Cannes, manager of Le Bal des Fous in Cannes, and assistant F&B outlet manager at Hôtel Barrière Le Normandy in Deauville.

He then led the restaurants of the Crans Ambassador in Crans-Montana, ran Beefbar at Lou Pinet in Saint-Tropez, and was F&B manager for Groupe Leitmotiv and Beefbar, before returning to Courchevel and to Barrière.

## The signal

In the Alps, a palace now lives as much from its restaurants as from its rooms. Entrusting several tables, from a Parisian trattoria to a caviar club, to a young director trained between the Riviera and the mountains shows how central F&B has become to the luxury winter season.

Congratulations to Grégoire Gaillard on his first winter season at Fouquet's Courchevel.
